summary.text: 好 is conventionally analyzed as 女 ‘woman’ with 子 ‘child’, an associative compound used for ‘good’. A mother–child idea has been proposed, but the graph’s original motivation is unresolved.

formation.text: A semantic (associative) compound of 女 and 子. The components support interpretations such as mother–child affection, but early uses do not directly confirm that proposal; beauty and man–woman affection are alternatives.

components.text: 女 ‘woman’ contributes to the conventional associative analysis of 好. Its presence does not determine whether the original idea concerned maternal affection, beauty, or another proposed motivation.
子 ‘child’ contributes to the conventional analysis. Early forms are described as showing it smaller than 女, favoring—but not proving—the mother–child interpretation.

history.text: Early forms are reported with 女 and 子 in variable positions; side-switched forms are treated as variants, not chronological ancestors. Some Warring States bamboo forms are reported with 丑 in place of 女. The sources do not establish a complete sequence of graphic change.

This oracle-script-style redraw arranges the forms vertically, while the bronze-script-style redraw places two forms side by side. These modern drawing layouts do not establish a sequence of change or the forms’ original component identities.

In the Shang name 婦好, a separate proposal treats 好 as a possible homograph: 子 may supply the sound and represent a lineage name. This name analysis does not establish a phonetic role for 子 in ordinary 好.

A bronze inscription is reported to use 好 as a phonetic loan for 孝. In a phonetic loan, a sign is reused for a different word because their spoken forms sound alike or similar; the account supplies no sound comparison, so the proposed match remains uncertain.

uncertainties.text: The original motivation of ordinary 好 remains unresolved. Proposed accounts include mother–child affection, a woman’s beauty, and affection between a man and woman; cited early uses do not directly attest the mother–child interpretation.
The supplied sources report the Shang personal name 婦好, but identify the earliest ordinary lexical use separately: a bronze example meaning ‘good/beautiful’ is reported without an absolute date.
Selected examples do not establish the order or transitions among ‘good’, ‘beautiful’, ‘friendly’, and ‘like’.
The reported phonetic loan for 孝 lacks an established sound comparison, so its proposed sound basis remains uncertain.

senses.text: A bronze inscription is reported with 好 meaning ‘good/beautiful’. The vessel is not absolutely dated in the account, so this example does not establish the earliest attested ordinary use.
A bronze inscription is reported with 好 in 好朋友, meaning ‘friendly’. Its chronological relation to the ‘good/beautiful’ use is not established.

A Warring States bamboo text is reported with 好 meaning ‘like’. A proposed Old Chinese suffixal relationship between the verbal reading and the ‘good’ reading does not establish which meaning came first.

In modern Chinese, 好 means ‘good’. The consulted dictionaries also list current adverbial uses meaning ‘very’ or ‘very much’; they do not establish a general standalone sense ‘well’. The evidence does not show the dated steps from the selected inscriptional uses to current usage.

limitations.text: The earliest ordinary lexical use and a complete semantic chronology are not established. The reported bronze ‘good/beautiful’ example is not absolutely dated.
The Shang name 婦好 is attested, but it remains unsettled whether its 好 is the same lexical graph and word as ordinary 好.

overview.text: 好 combines 女 ‘woman’ and 子 ‘child’ in a conventional associative analysis and commonly means ‘good’. Mother–child affection is one proposed original idea, but early uses do not directly confirm it.

components.text: 女 supplies the woman element in the conventional analysis; its presence does not settle the graph’s original idea.
子 supplies the child element; its smaller early form favors, but does not prove, the mother–child proposal.

items.caption: This oracle-script style redraw places two distinct forms vertically: an upper form with two enclosed spaces above a lower angular form with a long descending stroke. It illustrates one reported early layout of 好.
